before: StringBuilder stores a mutable sequence of characters. It is useful for assembling changing text without treating immutable String values as writable buffers.
append adds content to the builder. toString produces a String representing the builder’s current contents.
Changing the builder afterward does not modify a String already produced by toString. That String remains immutable.
This example uses one builder on one thread. StringBuilder is not a guarantee of thread-safe shared text updates.

Expected output or behavior: A
AB. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.
Optional local transfer task: Take a String snapshot before and after an append. Predict which values can still change. You may trace it without a JDK; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
after: Mutable means able to change. StringBuilder holds mutable text: you can add to the same builder. A String's text stays unchanged.
append adds text to the end of a builder. toString makes a String containing the builder's text at that moment, like a snapshot.
Changing the builder later does not change a String already made from it. The builder and the saved String can now hold different text.
A thread is a running sequence of instructions. This example uses one thread. StringBuilder alone does not protect its text when several threads change it together.
The program prints A, then AB on the next line. saved keeps the earlier text; builder includes the added letter.
The quiz changes only the letter passed to append. The snapshot is still taken before that addition.
